The appraised value is higher than predominant value however the comment on page# 12 says "It is noted that the subject's appraised valuation is below the predominant value for the neighborhood", please revise Paired Sales Analysis The appraiser utilized paired sales analysis which involves identifying two or more property sales that are highly similar in every aspect except the date of sale. By comparing the differences in sale prices, appraisers quantify the influence of changing market conditions. For example, if two identical properties sold six months apart at different prices, the price difference can help determine the percentage change due to market shifts. This approach works best when the properties have minimal other differences, allowing appraisers to isolate the effect of time. Appraisers can also segment comparable sales into specific time periods, like quarterly or monthly, to identify broader market trends. This method provides a clear, data-driven basis for supporting any time-related adjustments in an appraisal. When conducting paired sales analysis, it is important to ensure that the comparable properties used are as similar as possible. Which in this case all sales and comparables are similar in size, location, condition, bedroom as well as no basements and any unique features should be nearly identical to enhance the reliability of the analysis in isolating the effect of time. Paired sales analysis provides a straightforward, evidence-based way to derive time adjustments and is especially effective in stable markets with sufficient comparable sales. This method is valuable for demonstrating trends in smaller, localized markets where other techniques may be less applicable. Currently time adjustments are not warranted. All Utilities, appliances, Refrigerator and mechanicals were on and functioning of the effective date of this report. Carbon monoxide detectors were installed. The subject has been measured in compliance with ANSI Standard Z765-2021. To the knowledge of the appraiser the subject is not located near any drilling within 200 feet of the subject for oil, gas, and mineral leases. Appraised value is not at the predominant value. The subject is not an over or under improvement. It is noted that the subject's appraised valuation is ABOVE the predominant value for the neighborhood. The predominant value for the subject's neighborhood includes all homes and all sales, just not similar homes like the subject, or similar comparable sales to the subject. The subject neighborhood contains a very wide variety of properties in multiple price points. The predominant price shown on page 1 indicates the mode (most frequently occurring variate in a data set) for the neighborhood and has nothing to do the subject's relationship with the neighborhood or the relationship between the subject's value and the indicated predominant price. The subject's value is within the low-high price range for the neighborhood and does not automatically set the predominant. The appraisal includes all fixtures and articles that are now attached or appurtenant to the premises. The following search parameters were expanded to include sales and listings within 1.00 miles, 1-12 months, GLA +/- 10-50%, and age =/- 49-126 years. The search the above mentioned parameters expanded produced the following results, 4 sales and 1 active listings. Guidelines Exceeded: 1) Some comparables extended over major boundaries. Location adjustments were not necessary as these comparables are located in a similar market area as the subject. This does not effect the marketability of the subject property. 2) Some comparables exceeded the gla guideline. The appraiser utilized these sales due to there time of sale and to help bracket the final estimated value. These comparables are deemed valid value indicators. 3) Some comparables sold over three months from the date of the appraisal. This comparable is deemed a valid value indicator due to its classification. 4) Some comparables have unadjusted sales price exceeded the adjusted sales price by more than 15%. These comparables were utilized to help bracket the final estimated. 5) Age was exceeded by more than 5 years on comparables.Condition rather than age is adjusted in this market there is no discrepancy in age condition is adjusted. -:FINAL RECONCILIATION:- Most emphasis was placed on the sales comparison approach to value. The cost approach was given supportive consideration. The income {grm} approach was not considered as homes are normally not purchased for investment purposes. -:CONDITIONS OF APPRAISAL:- The intended user of this appraisal report is the lender/client.
